page: Amazon Web Services r6id.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA extensions. Memory capacity totals 384 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage is directly integrated, offering 2,850 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 19 Gbps baseline network connection.

Benchmark assessments locate the processor in the middle tier for raw multi-core compute, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,766 and a PassMark CPU score of 48,180.39. Cryptographic tasks demonstrate high efficiency, with the PassMark encryption test reaching the upper 25th percentile. Memory throughput tests demonstrate 163.75 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 70.15 GB/sec write bandwidth. In application-focused metrics, the system completed 44.66 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 38.7 GB/sec static web throughput, while small 135M model LLM prompt ingestion processed at 2,010.76 tokens per second.

The inclusion of large local NVMe storage balances the cost overhead of high memory capacity by providing low-latency scratch space without requiring additional network-attached volumes. Because the instance contains no GPU accelerators and exhibits moderate single-thread compute capabilities, it is not tailored for graphics or dedicated machine learning training. It provides a balanced hardware platform for in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, large relational databases, distributed analytics engines, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, powered by a 24-core Intel Xeon 8375C processor delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs at 3.5 GHz. Designed for memory-intensive workloads, it provides 384 GB of DDR4 RAM, maintaining an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU allocation. The hardware configuration bundles 2,850 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 19 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate solid memory bandwidth alongside top-quartile performance in cryptographic acceleration and image processing, achieving 44.66 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking GPU acceleration, the dense RAM footprint combined with integrated high-capacity NVMe storage makes this instance cost-effective and operationally efficient for large in-memory caches, operational databases, search indexing, and distributed data processing frameworks.
